newsitem.title: USA: GM strike, aircraft seen hurting Oct durable goods.
newsitem.headline: GM strike, aircraft seen hurting Oct durable goods.

text.p: For the second time this year, a strike at General Motors Corp looks to wreck havoc on government economic data.
First, it was a 17-day strike, idling a couple of dozen plants in March. And now the Canadian auto workers' strike last month has hit some October data.

Durable goods orders, due Wednesday at 1000 EST/1500 GMT, will be heavily affected. A Reuters poll showed economists predicted a 2.0-percent decline in durable goods orders in October after a rise of 4.9 percent in September.
Some economists forecast an even larger 2.5-percent fall.

The main culprit: an expected 7.0-percent decline in motor vehicle output, mostly due to the Canadian Auto Workers (CAW) strike. In addition, a projected 25-percent drop in civilian aircraft orders and an 8.0-percent fall in defense should depress data. Orders ex-defense are seen down 2.2 percent.

Economists, however, said forecasting durable goods orders is tough. "There's no way to be really educated on this number," said John McAuley, economist at Zions First National Bank. "But (for October), we know the wrinkle about auto production and orders."
Excluding transportation, durables orders are forecast to have risen about 0.5 percent in October on what analysts see are strong data processing orders.
Bill Sharp, economist at Smith Barney Inc, said orders outside of defense and transportation should be weak as well.
He also noted that defense orders tend to decrease in October -- the first month of the government's fiscal year -- falling in five of the last seven years.
Meanwhile, the overall number could be determined by aircraft orders, which surged 127 percent in September.
"It's asking a lot for aircraft to be up two months in a row," McAuley said.

"While Boeing (Co's orders look strong (in October), aircraft orders appear less than in September," said Cheryl Katz, economist at Merrill Lynch and Co Inc. "What happens with aircraft is what happens to the number."

The report will be released an hour and a half after its usual 0830 EST/1330 GMT time, since the Commerce Department is also releasing its revised third-quarter gross domestic product at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.
